description: Pull values out of the page source of every website in a cluster: organization names, contacts, social profiles, addresses, languages, registration numbers, analytics and tag ids - anything a regular expression can match. Easiest: fields - name (organization name and kind of business from schema.org markup); social (social profile links, regional networks too (VK, Weibo, Naver...)); email (email addresses: mailto: links, schema.org, addresses hidden by Cloudflare); phone (phone numbers: tel: links and schema.org); messengers (messenger links: WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber, LINE, KakaoTalk, WeChat, Messenger, Signal, Zalo, Threema); address (postal address from schema.org markup and map coordinates (embedded maps, geo tags)); apps (app store links: Google Play, App Store, AppGallery, Microsoft Store, RuStore, Galaxy Store, Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons); languages (languages of the pages, ISO 639 codes (html lang, hreflang)); registration (company registration and tax numbers: VAT, HRB, SIREN/SIRET, KvK, CNPJ, ABN, ИНН/ОГРН, ICP and more). Single networks by name - presets: email, phone, whatsapp, telegram, viber, line, facebook, instagram, x, linkedin, youtube, tiktok, pinterest, threads, bluesky, discord, github, google_play, app_store. Or write regex: PCRE in slashes, the first capture group is the value (with no group, the whole match), e.g. /data-site-id="([0-9]+)"/i. Up to 10 presets and expressions, one column each; fields add their columns. Works through the cluster in parts of up to 100 domains: call again with offset = next_offset until it is null. Costs extraction points: a website found in the index costs 1 point if anything was found, 0.1 if nothing; the account tool shows the daily allowance. It reads every indexed page of a website, not only the home page. Every call is paid for, a repeat of the same websites too: keep the answer and go on from next_offset. The REST API gives the same as a file (format=csv). A worked example, from a niche to contacts: the read_docs page clusters/example-contacts.

cluster.description: Cluster id, from list_clusters or create_cluster.

fields.description: Groups of values, a column or two each, e.g. ["name", "email", "phone", "address"].

include_empty.description: Also list websites where nothing matched.

limit.description: Domains to go through in this call.

offset.description: Where to start in the cluster; next_offset from the previous call.

presets.description: Single networks by name, e.g. ["whatsapp", "linkedin"]. Presets and regex together: up to 10.

name: extract_from_cluster
title: Extract data from a cluster
